chunks: Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

If a man forgets a salat (prayer), or performs it without taharah (ritual purity), while he is resident or traveling, then remembers it, he must make up what became obligatory upon him, neither adding to that nor subtracting. And whoever forgets four, he makes up four when he remembers it, whether he is traveling or resident. And if he forgets two rakʿahs, he performs two rakʿahs when he remembers it, whether he is traveling or resident.

key_terms.أَرْبَعًا: a four-rakʿah prayer to be made up as four
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: a two-rakʿah prayer to be made up as two
key_terms.صَلَاةً: an obligatory prayer that was missed or invalidly performed
key_terms.طَهُورٍ: ritual purity required for the validity of salat (prayer)
key_terms.فَلْيَقْضِ: he must perform the make-up of the missed obligation
key_terms.مُسَافِرًا: being in the state of travel
key_terms.مُقِيمًا: being in the state of residence
key_terms.وَجَبَ: became obligatory upon him in its original form

ai.seo_question: How should a missed prayer be made up if it was forgotten during travel or residence?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on making up missed salat (prayer) or a prayer performed without taharah (ritual purity). The qaḍāʾ must match the originally obligated prayer exactly, without increase or decrease, whether one remembers while traveling or resident.
